question_text: What distinguishes optimal substructure from overlapping subproblems in dynamic programming problem formulation?

options.text: Optimal substructure means subproblems share identical memory, while overlapping subproblems means greedy choice applies
Optimal substructure means an optimal solution to the problem contains optimal solutions to its subproblems; overlapping subproblems means the recursive solution tree recomputes identical states
Optimal substructure applies only to trees; overlapping subproblems apply only to graphs
They are synonymous terms describing iterative tabulations

answer_explanation: Optimal substructure allows global optimality to be built inductively from optimal sub-solutions (e.g. Bellman's principle), while overlapping subproblems make caching/memoization efficient by avoiding redundant tree branch evaluation.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Optimal substructure allows global optimality to be built inductively from optimal sub-solutions (e.g. Bellman's principle), while overlapping subproblems make caching/memoization efficient by avoiding redundant tree branch evaluation.
